hero.subtitle: When someone in Ross dies because another person or company was careless, the family left behind has a civil path forward under California law. We can help you understand your options at no cost.

about.title: Ross Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Ross is a small place. With fewer than 2,500 residents and streets like Ross Common and Loma Linda Avenue that most neighbors know by heart, a death here is felt by the whole town. In 2025, public records show two injury collisions in Ross, three people hurt, and no traffic fatalities. Still, sudden loss reaches small towns too. People from Ross drive Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, work and travel across Marin County, and can lose someone to a crash elsewhere, a medical error, an unsafe property, or a defective product. California law lets a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or child bring a civil wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other situations. The claim is separate from any criminal case and generally must be filed within two years of the death, sooner if a public agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death cases on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, giving priority to a spouse, domestic partner, and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can tell you where your family fits before anyone files paperwork.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched for you
items.desc: Most California wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting started early keeps those deadlines from slipping by during a hard season.

items.title: The full picture of what was lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Our job is to make sure none of that is left out.

items.question: Ross recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that affect whether my family has a claim?
items.answer: Not at all. A wrongful death claim depends on how and why your loved one died, not on where the town's yearly numbers stand. Many Ross families lose someone on a road outside city limits, in a hospital, or in an incident that never involved a vehicle. We look at the specific facts of your loss, not the local crash count.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as the criminal case against the person responsible?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil claim brought by the family, while a criminal case is brought by the district attorney on behalf of the state. The two proceed separately, and your civil claim can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed. The standards of proof are also different.

items.question: What does it cost to hire your team?
items.answer: Our initial consultation is free. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, which means no fee unless there is a recovery. You can ask us to explain our exact percentage and case costs before you agree to anything.
